title: Classroom Pre-Flight Check
persona: Mr. Davis, Middle School Science Teacher
scenario: Mr. Davis stops by the IT office before school. Tomorrow is the first day of a new science unit and he wants to be sure the classroom is ready. The room (rm. 207) has a ceiling projector, a wall input plate with HDMI and USB-C, a teacher MacBook, a document camera, classroom speakers, and a wireless microphone. He wants help running through a 'pre-flight check' so nothing fails in front of 25 sixth-graders.
impact: Instructional: A new science unit starts tomorrow for 25 sixth-graders. If the classroom technology fails during the lesson, the teacher loses the day and the students miss the planned hands-on demonstration.
objectives: Walk the room systematically and verify each technology component
Document any issues found before they impact teaching
Fix the smallest, easiest problems in the moment
Escalate anything that requires parts, change windows, or vendors
Hand the teacher a 'pre-flight checklist' to use independently next time
Document the visit and any follow-up tickets opened

evidence.description: Completed pre-flight checklist signed off by the technician and the teacher
Any issues found — failed component, loose cable, missing adapter
Any follow-up tickets opened for issues that could not be fixed in-room

decisionPoints.prompt: What is the best approach to the pre-flight walkthrough?

options.label: Use a written pre-flight checklist covering every component, verify each in order, and have the teacher sign off
options.feedback: Correct — a structured checklist ensures nothing is skipped and gives the teacher a tool to use independently next time.

options.label: Just look at the room and confirm everything looks right
options.feedback: Visual inspection alone misses issues that only show up at power-on (no signal, dead battery, failed network). A powered test is required.

options.label: Skip the checklist, do the test yourself, and tell the teacher the room is ready
options.feedback: Faster today, but the teacher cannot repeat the check tomorrow. A checklist builds teacher independence.

decisionPoints.prompt: The pre-flight finds: projector works, MacBook mirrors correctly, speakers work, but the wireless microphone will not pair. What is the correct action?

options.label: Document the mic issue, swap in a loaner mic from IT stock, and open a follow-up ticket to repair the original
options.feedback: Correct — restore the teacher's working state today (loaner mic) and follow up on the broken unit so the underlying issue is resolved.

options.label: Note the issue and tell the teacher to teach without the mic for tomorrow's lesson
options.feedback: The mic is part of the room's standard kit. Ignoring it means the teacher cannot use the equipment tomorrow as planned.

options.label: Order a brand-new mic and wait for it to arrive before the lesson
options.feedback: Ordering a new mic does not help tomorrow. A loaner from existing stock restores service now.

ticket.initialDescription: Pre-flight classroom technology check for rm. 207. New science unit starts tomorrow. Verify display, audio, mic, doc cam, network.

nodes.title: Greet and plan
nodes.body: Greet Mr. Davis. Confirm the goal: verify all classroom tech is ready for tomorrow's new science unit. Open a request ticket. Plan the walkthrough order.

nodes.title: Choose the approach
nodes.body: How will you run the pre-flight?

nodes.title: Walk the room and verify each component
nodes.body: Verify each item on the checklist: projector on and showing the MacBook, speakers audible, doc camera preview, Wi-Fi on the MacBook, network drive reachable. Save the completed checklist to the ticket.

nodes.title: Address the mic issue
nodes.body: The wireless microphone will not pair. What is the correct action?

nodes.title: Restore service with a loaner
nodes.body: Swap in a known-good loaner mic from IT stock, pair it with the receiver, and confirm audio works. Open a follow-up ticket to repair or replace the original mic.

nodes.title: Validate end-to-end
nodes.body: Have Mr. Davis run through his planned lesson flow: open lesson plan, mirror to projector, share audio through the speakers, demonstrate with the doc cam, use the mic. Confirm everything works for the planned demo.

nodes.title: Document and follow up
nodes.body: Save the completed checklist to the ticket. Document the loaner mic and the open follow-up ticket for the broken mic. Hand Mr. Davis a printed copy of the checklist for future use.
nodes.prompt: Write a brief follow-up to Mr. Davis summarizing what was checked, the loaner mic, and the open follow-up for the broken unit.

nodes.title: Debrief
nodes.body: Review your score. Consider how a pre-flight checklist can be standardized across the school so any teacher can run one independently.

kbOpportunity: A pre-flight checklist for every classroom — display, audio, mic, doc cam, network — catches issues before they reach students. Pair the check with a loaner pool so service is restored same-day.
